summary: In December 2024, Embodied announced it was closing and that its cloud-connected Moxie robots for children would soon stop functioning. Moxie had been used as an interactive companion and social-learning toy. Families described children’s distress at saying goodbye to robots they had formed attachments to; parents also faced the loss of a costly device and service. Later efforts to keep some robots functioning do not erase the initial shutdown and its effects on affected families.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The AIAAIC registry and contemporaneous reporting describe Embodied’s closure, anticipated cessation of Moxie’s cloud service and children’s reported grief. The reports support child-facing relational and educational functions and the shutdown’s immediate effect; they do not measure duration or clinical severity of individual distress. The purchase price illustrates an asset/service issue but does not establish unrecovered net loss for every family. Subsequent community continuity efforts may have differed by device and household.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Embodied’s closure ended the original Moxie service and disrupted child users’ companion interactions. The reported distress gives the exit decision a relational dimension, but the evidence does not establish a specific VIGIL failure class such as deliberate dependency optimisation or repurposing protected child signals. The record shows an end-of-service governance problem whose causal mechanism and transition obligations require separate evidence.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: A companion service can create relational expectations in children even when sold as a learning toy. Governance of such deployments includes foreseeable service endings, communication to families and an orderly transition path for established relationships and purchased devices.
